title: Grain boundary engineering using metallomesogen in formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide for stable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells - Nature Energy
text:
AbstractFormamidinium (FA)-doped caesium lead triiodide, Cs(FA)PbI3, is a promising front-cell absorber for tandem solar cells owing to its good stability, yet obtaining high-quality films remains a challenge. Here we identify that sparse doping of oversized FA cations induces severe grain boundary (GB) distortion, thereby facilitating defect generation and performance deterioration. To mitigate this, we develop a Pb-based metallomesogen that forms a mesophase exhibiting both solid-like and liquid-like properties. The phase characteristics enable the Pb-based metallomesogen to distribute uniformly along GBs of Cs(FA)PbI3 film, alleviating GB distortion, relieving shear strain, preserving lattice integrity and mitigating defect formation. Consequently, perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells based on a 1.66-eV Cs(FA)PbI3 absorber incorporating a Br-containing GB modifier achieve a champion efficiency of 32.08% (certified 31.62%), retaining 95% of the initial performance after ~3,000 h under maximum power point tracking and 93% after 1,500 h under 85% relative humidity and 85 °C damp-heat stressing.
